dialogue.Introduction: Oh! Um. H-hello. I'm Truffle. I live down in the basement under the carpenter's shop, where it's dim and damp and the mushrooms don't mind how quiet I am.$u
dialogue.Mon: Mondays are slow down here. The glowing caps only brighten up when someone visits, so maybe you could come by sometime?
dialogue.Tue: I was supposed to tidy the spore jars today. Instead I sat and listened to the pipes gurgle. Quite nice, actually.
dialogue.Wed: Wednesday. The Mechanic keeps tapping on the floor above me, and I can hear every hammer strike. I don't mind. It's like a little heartbeat.
dialogue.Thu: Thursday, and the cave mushrooms are sprouting again. Back in the mushroom biome I counted them to fall asleep.
dialogue.Fri: Friday is market day in town, and I really ought to go. But the crowds are so loud. Maybe I'll just grow a bit more today.
dialogue.Sat: Saturday. The valley sounds so bright from up there, all birds and chatter. I like listening to it through the floorboards.$h
dialogue.Sun: Sundays are for mending. I've been patching a hole in my spore hat. The Steampunker says it looks dashing. I'm not sure.
dialogue.Mon4: Oh, @, you came down again. I didn't tidy the room, so please ignore the mess and the mushroom in the corner. I call him Old Spot.$h
dialogue.Tue4: I made you a little glowing charm to keep the bats away. It's a bit lumpy, sorry. I'd like you to keep it anyway.$h
dialogue.Wed4: The Mechanic says I'm a fine hand with a bellows. Wednesday is when I feel most useful, helping with someone's lamp.$h
dialogue.Thu4: Sometimes the silence down here gets heavy. Then you knock on the trapdoor and it all lifts right up. Thank you for that.$h
dialogue.Fri4: I bought fresh spores from the Stardrop Saloon for you, but I got too shy and left them on the counter. Next time I'll hand them over myself.$s
dialogue.Sat4: The Steampunker says I should go to the Calico Desert for some sunshine. I'd dry up like a raisin in a day. I'd still go, if you came along.$h
dialogue.Sun4: Sunday evenings are my favourite. We could sit by the lamp and share a cup of tea, and I wouldn't feel so small in the dark.$l
dialogue.Mon8: There was a time I thought I'd always be alone in the glowing caves. Then you walked into my basement. I think about that every morning now.$l
dialogue.Tue8: Please don't laugh, but I wrote a poem about your farm. It is terrible. I'd rather read it to you than let it rot in a drawer.$l
dialogue.Wed8: The Mechanic keeps teasing me about you. She says I light up like a glowing mushroom when you're near. I suppose that's a fair description.$l
dialogue.Thu8: I used to dream the valley would be scary, full of loud people and sharp tools. Instead I found a farm with you in it, and that's the best dream I've had.$l
dialogue.Fri8: When the goblins came, I was terrified, but I kept thinking about your fields and your smile. It made my spores stand up straight.$h
dialogue.Sat8: Could you stay a while tonight? I know I'm quiet, mushroom-scented company, but I'd like it more than anything.$l
dialogue.Sun8: Whatever the seasons bring, I hope they always bring you back down these stairs. The cellar is only bright when you're in it.$l
dialogue.danceRejection: Oh! Um, a dance? With me? I'd step on your toes twice before the first song ended. Ask me again when I've stopped hiding behind the pumpkin crates.$s
dialogue.Mon2: Back so soon? I put the kettle on. It only whistles a little. Don't worry about the steam.$h
dialogue.Sat2: Saturday visitors are rare down here. You're welcome to sit on the old barrel. It's sturdier than it looks.$h
dialogue.Sun2: Sunday again. I'm trying to learn everyone's role in town. So far I know the Mechanic, the Steampunker and you. Good start, I think.$h
dialogue.Thu2: Thursday is when the fungus tries to escape the jars. I keep a little broom just for it. Please don't ask me to explain the jars.
dialogue.Tue6: Do you think mushrooms can feel lonely? I'd like to believe they're happier with company. Maybe that's why I talk to them so much.$s
dialogue.Wed6: You've seen the basement now, and you're still here. Most folks take one look at the glowing caps and run off to the saloon.$h
dialogue.Sun6: I've been thinking of baking a mushroom pie for the Luau. If the soup needs something earthy, I'll be there with a bowl.$h
dialogue.Fri10: Friday nights I used to spend counting my spores, alone. Now I'd rather count the minutes until you visit. That's dreadfully sweet of me, isn't it?$l
dialogue.Wed10: I think the Mechanic was right. The lamp in the corner is brighter now than it ever was. I suppose that's because you keep coming down the stairs.$l
dialogue.spring_Tue: Spring rain brings the little spring mushrooms up through the floorboards. I'm going to pretend they're flowers so the Mechanic doesn't complain.$h
dialogue.summer_Sat: The summer sun makes the cellar dry and cozy, but I still prefer the cool shade of the old mines.$h
dialogue.fall_Mon: Autumn is my favourite season for mushrooms. The forest floor is covered in them. Would you come picking with me this weekend?$h
dialogue.winter_Sun: Snow up top, lamplight down here. I have a jar of cocoa and two cups. Would you share one with me, @?$l
dialogue.winter_Fri8: When the ice cracks on the pond, I think of the caves below it. Every hidden thing waiting to be found. That's how I feel about you.$l
dialogue.spring_9: The ninth day of spring, and the first flowers are out on the farm. I'd dance in the field if I weren't so clumsy.$h
dialogue.fall_15: Harvest season smells of earth and mushrooms. I can't help grinning. Not that I smell like anything but spores, sadly.$h
dialogue.winter_20: A quiet winter day is a good day to tidy the cellar. I'm tidying the whole cellar except one corner, which is for you.$l
dialogue.summer_3: Summer evenings are warm and pleasant for once. I might even stay out past dusk, if somebody holds the lantern.

rainy: Rain on the carpenter's roof drips straight through the cellar ceiling. The mushrooms love it, but I just keep a bucket by the stairs.

marriage.Indoor_Day_0: Good morning, @. Shall we share the lamp for breakfast today?$l
marriage.Indoor_Day_1: Hm? Oh, you're up already. I'm only sorting the spore jars. Come sit with me, love.
marriage.Indoor_Day_2: The house is warm, and you're in it. That's my favourite kind of afternoon.$h
marriage.Indoor_Day_3: I've swept the cellar twice, @. Would you like to inspect it? I left one dusty corner for you.$h
marriage.Indoor_Day_4: We have plenty of space here, but I still find myself sitting closest to you.$l
marriage.Rainy_Day_0: Rain on the roof again. I'll make the tea if you bring the blankets.
marriage.Rainy_Day_1: Listen to the drips. The bucket keeps time for us, @.$h
marriage.Rainy_Day_2: A rainy day is the best excuse to stay in and be cozy with you.$l
marriage.Rainy_Day_3: The mushrooms are cheerful today. So am I, since you're here.$h
marriage.Rainy_Day_4: Stay in bed a little longer, @. The rain isn't going anywhere, and neither am I.$l
marriage.Indoor_Night_0: Goodnight, @. The lamp will stay on for you. It always does.$l
marriage.Indoor_Night_1: Are you sleeping? No? Good. Neither am I. Let's count the glowing caps together.$h
marriage.Indoor_Night_2: The cellar is dark, but your face makes it bright. I think I'll miss the lamp for one night.$l
marriage.Indoor_Night_3: Come to bed, love. The mushrooms can keep watch tonight.$l
marriage.Indoor_Night_4: Thank you for another lovely evening, @. I'm too happy to say it properly, so I'm just going to hold your hand.$l
marriage.Rainy_Night_0: Rain on the cellar door tonight. I'm glad you're tucked in beside me.$h
marriage.Rainy_Night_1: I could listen to the rain forever with you here, @.$l
marriage.Rainy_Night_2: Stormy nights used to scare me. Now I just hold on to you and count the thunder.$h
marriage.Rainy_Night_3: The bucket by the stairs is full again, but I wouldn't leave this bed for anything.$l
marriage.Rainy_Night_4: We're cozy, the lamp is low and the rain is soft. Goodnight, @.$h
marriage.Outdoor_0: What a lovely walk. The forest path smells of moss and rain, and you're holding my hand.$h
marriage.Outdoor_1: Careful on the stones, @. I don't want you to slip. Or me, honestly.$u
marriage.Outdoor_2: Look at the sun on the wheat. Doesn't it make you want to stay out forever?$h
marriage.Outdoor_3: I brought a little basket for mushrooms, just in case we find a patch.$h
marriage.Outdoor_4: You know, the valley is a little less frightening every day, with you walking beside me.$l
marriage.Good_0: Morning, @. Your breakfast is on the table and it isn't burnt. I checked twice.$h
marriage.Good_1: You look wonderful today, @. Have you been practising your smile?$l
marriage.Good_2: Shall we tidy the cellar together? I'd like the company, and you know I'm terrible at lifting boxes.$h
marriage.Good_3: I finished the mushroom pie, @. I was too scared to taste it, so you'll have to try first.$h
marriage.Good_4: I'm glad we live here together. Every corner of this house feels a little more like ours.$l
marriage.Good_5: Do you know how much I love hearing you hum while you cook? I'm listening right now.$l
marriage.Good_6: The glowing caps are looking very handsome today. Maybe that's just my pride talking.$h
marriage.Good_7: I was thinking of you while I trimmed the spore lamps. Silly, I know, but you're always on my mind.$l
marriage.Good_8: There is nowhere in the valley I'd rather be than right here, with you, @.$l
marriage.Good_9: I'm so proud of the farm you've built. I'm prouder still of the person who built it.$l
marriage.Neutral_0: Mm, yes. The spores need watering and the stew needs salt. Could you grab the salt?
marriage.Neutral_1: Did you move the spore jars again? No? Strange. They keep wandering off.$u
marriage.Neutral_2: The Mechanic is hammering again. I'm going to pretend it isn't happening.$s
marriage.Neutral_3: I'm a bit tired today, @. Would you mind doing the dishes? I'll make it up to you.$s
marriage.Neutral_4: The farm is busy and so is the cellar. I'm busy being quietly in love with you.$h
marriage.Neutral_5: I'm not in the mood for chatter today. But you can sit there. That's allowed.$s
marriage.Neutral_6: Let's just sit for a while. Sometimes silence is the nicest thing to share.$h
marriage.Neutral_7: I'm happy, I think. I'm just not very good at saying so yet.$s
marriage.Neutral_8: I've been quiet today. It isn't you. It's the damp and the stairs and my nerves.$s
marriage.Neutral_9: Ah, @. Oh good, you're here. I was just about to be grumpy about the cellar.$h
marriage.Bad_0: Don't leave the spore jars open again, @. The whole room smells like wet socks.$a
marriage.Bad_1: I know you didn't mean it, but please mind the stairs. I nearly fell down them.$s
marriage.Bad_2: I'm not cross, I'm just tired of tripping over the mop bucket.$a
marriage.Bad_3: You woke me again. I'm not angry. I'm mostly sleepy.$a
marriage.Bad_4: Let's talk about the dishes later, @. Right now my nerves are fried.$s
marriage.Bad_5: Not now. Please. I need a moment to breathe in the dark.$s
marriage.Bad_6: Boots on the carpet again? Honestly.$a
marriage.Bad_7: I'd rather not argue. Take the lamp and give me some quiet, alright?$s
marriage.Bad_8: I feel silly, but I'm upset. Please just sit beside me without saying anything.$s
marriage.Bad_9: We're fine. We're fine. I just need the cellar to stop spinning for a minute.$s
marriage.OneKid_0: Look, @, %kid1 has found a glowing mushroom in the corner. It's bigger than their head.$h
marriage.OneKid_1: %kid1 keeps asking if we can grow a cave garden. I said yes before you could say no.$h
marriage.OneKid_2: %kid1 is sitting in my lap reading. I think they got my shyness, poor thing.$l
marriage.OneKid_3: Our little one is wonderful, @. Just like you. Please don't tell them I cried.$l
marriage.TwoKids_0: %kid1 and %kid2 are racing around the cellar. I'm trying to stop them before they knock over the jars.$h
marriage.TwoKids_1: The two of them have built a fort out of hay bales. I'm not sure I can fix it, but I love it.$h
marriage.TwoKids_2: I counted two little pairs of boots by the stairs. Two! I'm so proud, @.$l
marriage.TwoKids_3: %kid1 and %kid2 asked me for a lullaby. I know one. It's about mushrooms. Don't laugh.$l
marriage.NoBed_0: There's no bed in the cellar yet, @. We'll have to take turns on the old barrel.$s
marriage.NoBed_1: Sorry, the bed is still upstairs. I'll bring the mattress down tomorrow, I promise.$s
marriage.NoBed_2: You can have the quilt tonight, @. I'll keep warm with a jar of spores.$h
marriage.NoBed_3: I found a blanket, a pillow and you. That's all a bed needs, I think.$l
marriage.patio_Sebastian: The patio is lovely in the sun. Let's sit out and watch the valley, @.$h
marriage.spouseRoom_Sebastian: Our room is my favourite place, @. The quilt is soft and you're the best part of it.$l
marriage.funLeave_Sebastian: I'm off to the mines for a bit. Look after the lamp while I'm gone, alright?$h
marriage.funReturn_Sebastian: I'm home! Did you miss me? I missed you the whole walk back.$l
marriage.Outdoor_Sebastian: Out here you look like a sunflower, @. Shall we take the long way home?$h
marriage.spring_Sebastian: Spring has come to the valley, and so have you, right into my heart. Quite poetic, sorry.$l
marriage.summer_Sebastian: Summer nights and warm cellars. I could get used to this season, love.$h
marriage.fall_Sebastian: Autumn leaves on the cellar steps. I swept them up, and then I left a few there for you.$l
marriage.winter_Sebastian: Winter is cold, but you keep the fire burning, @. Stay close and warm me up.$l

situations.eye: The big eye in the sky is gone. I was so frightened of it that I stayed under my blanket for two days. Thank you for chasing it off, @.$s
situations.evilBoss: Something from the deep caves crawled out last night. It was horrid. I'm glad you were brave enough to stop it, @.$s
situations.skeletron: The old dungeon is open now, and the Old Man came back to say hello. I've never seen so many bones in one place. Please be careful down there.$u
situations.queenBee: The bees went quiet last night after their Queen fell. I felt bad for them. They were only protecting their hive.$s
situations.hardmode: Hardmode. Everything glows brighter and nastier now. The Hallow is spreading and my mushrooms are scared. Stay close to the lamp, @.$u
situations.mechs: One of those big metal monsters was destroyed last night. The Mechanic cheered so loudly I heard her through the floor.$h
situations.plantera: Plantera is gone and the jungle temple is open. The flowers there are beautiful, but I'd rather stay here with my mushrooms.$h
situations.golem: The stone idol in the jungle has fallen. The Mechanic says it's the greatest thing she has ever seen. I think she's just pleased she didn't have to fix it.$h
situations.cultist: The Lunatic Cultist is gone and the pillars are out in the sky. I can see them glowing through my little cellar window. Stay safe up there, @.$u
situations.moonLord: The Moon Lord fell last night. The whole valley went quiet. I hid behind the mushrooms until the sky turned blue again.$s
situations.goblins: The goblin army came through last night and got chased off. I was too frightened to peek out. Still, we all made it through.$s
situations.pirates: The pirates came crashing up the coast last night. I stayed in the cellar with a lamp. Thankfully the Pirate was on our side for once.$u
situations.frostLegion: The Frost Legion was driven back last night. The snowmen are still standing guard by the pond, and frankly they're rather cute.$h
situations.martians: Martians in the sky last night! Their saucers lit up the whole valley. I hid under the stairs and counted to a thousand, twice.$u
situations.bloodMoon: There was a blood moon last night. The red light crept under my door and every mushroom in the cellar went quiet. I didn't sleep a wink.$s
situations.eclipse: The sun went dark today. The mushrooms thought it was night and started glowing. Honestly, I did too, a little.$u
situations.party: The Party Girl is throwing a party today. Everyone is invited, even quiet cellar folk like me. I might come up for one dance. Maybe.$h

festivals.spring13: Egg Festival! I painted my little spore egg in the most gloriously ugly colours. The Mechanic says it looks like a bruise. I think it's fine.$h
festivals.spring24: The Flower Dance is tonight. I'd love to dance with someone, but my feet have a mind of their own. Maybe we can just stand together and watch the petals.$s
festivals.summer11: The Luau! I brought a mushroom soup for the big community pot. Please don't tell anyone it came from the basement. They'll think it has been growing down there.$h
festivals.summer28: The Dance of the Moonlight Jellies is tonight. The glowing jellyfish remind me of my cap lights. I'd like to watch them with you on the sand.$l
festivals.fall16: The Stardew Valley Fair! I entered a mushroom display in the grange. It won a star token, which is more than I expected. You should see the blue ribbon.$h
festivals.fall27: Spirit's Eve! The haunted maze is far too spooky for me, but my mushrooms make the perfect costume. Don't scream when you see me coming around the corner.$h
festivals.winter8: Festival of Ice! The ice fishing is lovely, but I spend most of my time keeping my toes warm. A hot mug and a seat by the fire would suit me very well.$h
festivals.winter25: Feast of the Winter Star! I wrapped a gift for you in soft paper and hid it under the stairs. Please don't peek until the party is over.$l
festivals.spring13_spouse: Egg Festival, and this year I'm not hiding. You're my spouse, so we're painting an egg together, @. Let's make a glorious mess.$l
festivals.spring24_spouse: Flower Dance! Dancing with my spouse is the only dance I've ever wanted. Hold my hand and I promise I won't step on your toes. Much.$l
festivals.summer11_spouse: Luau soup, and this year we brew it together. One pot, two bowls. That's a marriage in my book.$l
festivals.summer28_spouse: The Moonlight Jellies are lovely tonight, but you're lovelier, @. I wouldn't trade a single glowing jelly for you.$l
festivals.fall16_spouse: The Fair! Our booth won a star token and I'm so proud I could burst. Our cellar mushrooms have finally made it out into the world.$h
festivals.fall27_spouse: Spirit's Eve. I'll walk the haunted maze with you, @, and I won't scream even once. Alright, twice.$h
festivals.winter8_spouse: Festival of Ice. Let's share a blanket and a mug of cocoa while we watch the snow sculptures. You keep me warm, @.$l
festivals.winter25_spouse: Feast of the Winter Star. I found the perfect present this year. It's a whole family of tiny mushrooms, and I'm going to name each one after you.$l

loved.text: A real truffle! @, you're far too kind. I'm going to keep this one in a little box forever.$l

liked.text: Oh, mushrooms! Lovely ones too. I'll set them beside the lamp so they can glow along with me.$h

neutral.text: Thank you, @. I'll find a safe place for it down here.

disliked.text: Oh... that's a bit loud for my cellar, @. I'll put it away before the mushrooms get nervous.$s

hated.text: Please, not near the caps! Take that away right now. I'm too frightened to be polite about it.$a

events.after: Please don't tell anyone I talk to the mushrooms. They're better listeners than most people.

steps.say: Oh! @! You startled me. I was only checking the spores.$s
Most people think this basement is creepy. I like it. Mushrooms never ask a lot of questions.$h

steps.question: Do you ever get lonely down here?

answers.reply: Oh... that's kind. I'm not used to kindness. It makes me all fluttery.$l
Hmph. Maybe. Then I'll keep the mushrooms and you can be the company.$a

steps.say: Here. A glowing cap I grew myself. It's bright all the way down the stairs, so don't drop it.$h

events.after: The Mechanic keeps poking at my pipes. Thank you for coming down to the cellar, @.

steps.say: Oh! @! Hello. The Mechanic is down here fixing the drain pipe, and she's humming, so she must be happy.$u
I was going to hide behind the mushroom crates until you left. Silly, isn't it?$s
Hide? Don't be silly, Truffle. Nobody on this farm bites, except the goats.
The Mechanic says I'm shy. I say I'm careful. We both know the truth, I suppose.$h
Keep the pipe straight, Truffle, and invite @ to dinner sometime.

steps.question: Would you like some mushroom stew?

answers.reply: Oh! Then I'll make it. Stay as long as you like. I'll hum along, too.$h
That's alright. The stew will wait, like I do.$s

events.after: Watch your step on the way home. The roots are sneaky, just like the shadows.

steps.say: @! You found the forest path. I come up here to pick mushrooms when the sun is kind.$h
See that cluster under the fern? Brown caps with white dots. That's the good kind. The other kind makes you dance until you fall over.$u
I used to be frightened of the forest. So many shadows, and so many things that might eat you. You walk through it like it's nothing.$l

steps.question: Are you ever scared in the forest?

answers.reply: Hey! That's a cruel joke. Sorry, I laughed anyway.$h
Company. That's a lovely word. I'm glad I'm someone you share it with.$l

steps.say: Here, a glowing cap for you. It lights the way home when the sun goes down.$h
Oh... @. You came down so late. I wasn't expecting anyone, so please excuse the mess.$u
I've been practising what to say to you all week. Every version sounds silly in my head.$s
So I'll just say the true one. I like you, @. More than the lamp and more than the mushrooms, and that's saying a lot.$l

steps.question: Would you like to go on a walk with me tomorrow?

answers.reply: Really? Oh, I'll bring a basket and all the courage I have.$l
Oh. That's alright. I'll wait for the next bright day.$s

steps.say: Thank you for listening to me. You make the whole cellar feel warm.$h
@, the waves are so loud tonight. I hope they don't drown out what I'm trying to say.$u
We've been close for ages, and I think I've been waiting for the perfect moment to ask you properly.$s
Forget perfect. I'm asking now. Would you be my sweetheart, @?$l

answers.reply: Oh! Oh my. I'm going to cry into my scarf, sorry.$l
Of course. I'll be right here by the water, waiting patiently. Mostly.$s

steps.say: Look, the moonlight is on the water. Glowing, like the caps in my cellar. I think you're my favourite light, @.$l

events.after: Let's never go back down to the cellar without holding hands.

steps.say: @, you're home. Come in, come in. I've set the table. Not with the mushroom centrepiece, I promise.$h
I still think about the day you first came down those cellar stairs. I was terrified, and I'm so glad you stayed.$l
Every morning since, you have been the warmest thing in my world. Thank you for choosing me, @.$l
I have a small gift for us. A little mushroom in a glass jar, glowing gently, just like we do.$h
Welcome home, love. I'm so happy you're mine.$l
